items.stem: ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING RESULTS — all samples collected under valid dynamic conditions. Which values EXCEED Massachusetts Board Policy 2026-03 action levels? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: ISO Class 7 viable-air sample: 10 CFU per 1,000 L.
choices.why: Incorrect. The policy lists action as greater than 10 CFU for ISO 7 viable air. Ten equals, rather than exceeds, that threshold.

choices.text: ISO Class 5 surface sample: 4 CFU per media device.
choices.why: Correct. The policy defines ISO 5 surface action as greater than 3 CFU; four exceeds it.

choices.text: ISO Class 8 surface sample: 50 CFU per media device.
choices.why: Incorrect. The ISO 8 surface action threshold is greater than 50 CFU, not equal to 50.

choices.text: ISO Class 7 non-viable air: 352,001 particles of at least 0.5 micrometer per cubic meter.
choices.why: Correct. The ISO 7 nonviable action threshold is greater than 352,000 particles; the result exceeds it.

items.novelty_rationale: Threshold >, not ≥, with different sample type and ISO class; older C questions focus on general CSP BUDs and sterility training.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: A sterile compounding pharmacy samples an ISO Class 5 PEC on Monday, November 9. The microbiology vendor's report showing an action-level viable result reaches its Manager of Record on Thursday, November 12, 2026. No holiday intervenes. By which date must the Board notification be made?

choices.text: Wednesday, November 11, based only on sample collection.
choices.why: Incorrect. The reporting clock is measured from receipt of the microbiology report, not when the sample was collected.

choices.text: Friday, November 13, one business day after receipt of the report.
choices.why: Correct. Policy 2026-03 §II specifies notice within one business day of receiving the microbiology report.

choices.text: Thursday, November 19, seven days after microbiology report receipt.
choices.why: Incorrect. The applicable Board policy has a one-business-day deadline, not a one-week deadline.

choices.text: Only after a second action-level sample confirms contamination.
choices.why: Incorrect. An action-level report triggers the notice; repeat sampling is part of follow-up remediation, not a prerequisite to notice.

items.novelty_rationale: Distinct specimen-collection and report-receipt clocks, rather than generic sterile-compounding records.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: A cleanroom operator proposes collecting routine environmental samples at 6:00 AM immediately after an overnight deep clean, before staff enter or compound, then using those results to establish that production conditions are controlled. Which corrections follow the Massachusetts Environmental Monitoring advisory and Policy 2026-03? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Use risk-based sampling under representative dynamic operating conditions that reflect compounding activity.
choices.why: Correct. The Board advisory requires dynamic conditions, including ongoing work and personnel, and the policy calls for a risk-based plan.

choices.text: Accept the after-deep-clean data as sufficient evidence because fewer organisms will be recovered.
choices.why: Incorrect. Sampling immediately after a deep clean fails to capture meaningful dynamic production conditions.

choices.text: Work with a microbiologist or other qualified professional to choose the appropriate sites, times and sampling locations.
choices.why: Correct. The Board policy and advisory explicitly require a risk-based plan developed with qualified technical assistance.

choices.text: Eliminate surface samples if the air sampler returns zero organisms.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board program encompasses viable air, surface, and nonviable air environmental monitoring as applicable.

items.citation: Board Policy 2026-03 §I; Board Environmental Monitoring Advisory §§I(A), II(A)
items.novelty_rationale: Addresses false reassurance from post-clean non-dynamic samples, not an existing BUD or gowning test.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: An ISO Class 7 sterile-compounding area has an action-level NON-VIABLE particle count, but viable cultures remain within limits. The manager initiates cleaning and proposes resuming routine Category 2 CSPs immediately, without completing remediation or recertifying the facility. No Board order changes the policy. Which response is correct?

choices.text: Resume at full BUD if microbial samples are acceptable; the nonviable result can be ignored.
choices.why: Incorrect. Policy 2026-03 separately regulates nonviable action-level excursions even if viable samples are acceptable.

choices.text: Use the policy's 24-hour room-temperature viable-excursion BUD to resume production in every affected room.
choices.why: Incorrect. Section V's conditional continuation rules do not replace the nonviable particle-count suspension provision.

choices.text: Resume once a corrective-action plan is written, even if the classified areas have not been recertified.
choices.why: Incorrect. For nonviable action-level counts, suspension continues until full remediation and recertification of all ISO classified areas.

choices.text: Suspend sterile compounding until fully remediated and all ISO-classified areas are recertified.
choices.why: Correct. Section III(D) explicitly requires suspension for nonviable action-level counts until full remediation and recertification, unless Board-directed otherwise.

items.novelty_rationale: Distinguishes nonviable mandatory suspension from conditional viable-area continuation.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy normally counts an intact, manufacturer-finished hazardous antineoplastic tablet using its documented handling policy. During fulfillment, several tablets break and powder escapes onto the work area. The worker proposes scooping them with bare hands because the order was not a compound. What is the appropriate response?

choices.text: Apply the pharmacy's hazardous-drug spill/exposure control procedure and trained staff protections.
choices.why: Correct. Physical damage and powder exposure require the HD program's handling, PPE, cleaning and spill controls rather than ordinary intact tablet counting.

choices.text: Handle the fragments like any intact tablet because the patient-specific order is not a compounded prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. The new exposure risk is not equivalent to handling the manufacturer-finished intact dosage form.

choices.text: Dispose of the powder in the regular sink to avoid further countertop handling.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board advisory requires appropriate HD waste segregation and spill remediation; drain disposal is not a safe general method.

choices.text: Count the remaining broken tablets on a shared tray after wiping the surface with a dry cloth.
choices.why: Incorrect. Uncontrolled powder contamination is incompatible with required hazardous-handling SOPs and worker protection.

items.citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies §§PPE, Handling, Spill Control, Waste; 247 CMR 9.01(3)
items.novelty_rationale: Escaped powder and contaminated-work-area response versus E30-140 intact antineoplastic assessment of risk and D-W1 workplace training.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is revising its hazardous-drug storage map. The inventory contains finished, intact antineoplastic tablets, reproductive-risk-only products, and an antineoplastic bulk material reserved for later manipulation. Which statements follow the Board's community-pharmacy advisory? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Intact finished antineoplastic dosage forms may be stored with other medication under a suitable pharmacy policy.
choices.why: Correct. The Board advisory permits storage with other medicine for final antineoplastic dosage forms, subject to the pharmacy's policies and procedures.

choices.text: Antineoplastic HDs requiring future manipulation must be handled under full USP <800> containment strategies.
choices.why: Correct. The advisory explicitly lists storage of antineoplastic drugs needing future manipulation among full-containment situations.

choices.text: All reproductive-risk-only finished products require the same storage containment as hazardous bulk API used for compounding.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board describes permitted co-storage of reproductive-risk-only products; it distinguishes API and manipulated antineoplastic conditions.

choices.text: A formal hazardous-drug program includes documented storage and handling procedures.
choices.why: Correct. The Board advisory calls for documented hazardous-drug storage, handling and related policies, including receipt, labeling and spill precautions.

items.citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies pp.1–3 (full containment cases, storage/handling)
items.novelty_rationale: Actual storage map differentiates intact antineoplastic products, reproductive-only risk and bulk for manipulation.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: A newly hired pharmacy receiver completed hazardous-drug handling training and an initial competency evaluation in October 2025. By November 2026, the employee continues independently receiving hazardous packages but has had no competency reassessment. Which policy requirement was missed?

choices.text: A mandatory pharmacist licensure examination taken every quarter.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board's hazardous handling competency expectation is function-based, not a quarterly pharmacist license exam.

choices.text: A new manufacturer shipping agreement signed by the worker each time a delivery arrives.
choices.why: Incorrect. Manufacturer shipping contracts do not substitute for documented employee HD handling competencies.

choices.text: Documented reassessment of hazardous-drug competencies at least every 12 months.
choices.why: Correct. The Board advisory specifies initial assessment and reassessment at least every 12 months for staff independently handling HDs.

choices.text: Annual DEA Schedule II inventory certification for every receiving employee.
choices.why: Incorrect. The HD worker competency requirement is distinct from DEA inventory obligations.

items.citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies §Training (p.3)
items.novelty_rationale: Function-specific worker competency expiration versus earlier technician ratio and ongoing pharmacist CE questions.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: A nonsterile HD pharmacy compounder uses a NIOSH-listed hazardous API in a containment powder hood. After HVAC repair the room has lost negative pressure. Management proposes an assessment of risk instead of fixing the engineering failure. What must occur before compounding resumes?

choices.text: Continue compounding after documenting a fresh product-specific assessment of risk.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board advisory states hazardous API compounding requires full containment; a reduced-containment risk assessment does not replace it.

choices.text: Continue if a second staff member verifies the weight of the hazardous ingredient.
choices.why: Incorrect. A checking step cannot restore missing environmental containment.

choices.text: Compound on an open weighing bench.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board identifies containment equipment in a negative-pressure room for hazardous compounding.

choices.text: Restore and verify negative-pressure containment before compounding resumes.
choices.why: Correct. The pharmacy cannot substitute a reduced AOR for a missing negative-pressure containment system that is required for this manipulation.

items.citation: Board Advisory: USP <800> in Community Pharmacies pp.1–2 (C-PEC in negative pressure), 247 CMR 9.01(3)
items.novelty_rationale: A failed engineering environment is the decisive change, rather than merely asking which HD preparations require containment.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: A 503A pharmacy considers an automated nonsterile compounder with no documented FDA approval. What does the Massachusetts Board's November 2025 memorandum require the pharmacy to check?

choices.text: Reject it because every device requires FDA clearance.
choices.why: Incorrect. The memorandum permits a documented manufacturer-validation pathway where FDA approval is not required or applicable.

choices.text: Check FDA approval requirements or documented manufacturer validation for the device.
choices.why: Correct. The Board memo asks the pharmacy to assess FDA approval status or other manufacturer validation documentation for nonsterile compounding.

choices.text: Use the device because a vendor advertises it as 'automated,' without checking validation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Marketing claims alone do not satisfy the pharmacy's documentation responsibility.

choices.text: Rely solely on a pharmacist's current license instead of reviewing device validation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Pharmacist credentials do not replace equipment validation and compounding-quality requirements.

items.citation: MA Board Memorandum 2025-11-06: Automated Non-Sterile Compounding Devices ¶1
items.novelty_rationale: Device approval-required versus verified manufacturer validation, not old E30-095 distinction between 503A and 503B dispensing models.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.

items.stem: An automatic nonsterile compounder is manufacturer-validated. Its compatibility file lists ingredient X for an approved IND study, but FDA-approved API Y is absent. Which statements follow the Board's 2025 memorandum? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The pharmacy must confirm that each applicable FDA-approved API or approved-IND ingredient is compatible with the device.
choices.why: Correct. The memo imposes a separate ingredient compatibility check beyond equipment validation.

choices.text: Manufacturer device validation alone establishes compatibility for every possible substance.
choices.why: Incorrect. The Board's second item requires independent confirmation of component compatibility.

choices.text: Ingredient Y may be used without further review because its parent drug received FDA approval.
choices.why: Incorrect. FDA approval of an API does not itself demonstrate compatibility with the selected device.

choices.text: Ingredient Y should not be used until the pharmacy confirms device compatibility for that ingredient.
choices.why: Correct. A validated machine does not establish the safety or suitability of an unverified API on the ingredient-specific check.

items.citation: MA Board Memorandum 2025-11-06: Automated Non-Sterile Compounding Devices ¶¶1–2
items.novelty_rationale: Equipment validation exists but a new FDA-approved API is absent from compatibility evidence.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational questions; not real secure MPJE items.
